key_terms.meaning: Frequency where gain falls to 1/√2 of its passband value; for a first-order RC filter, fc = 1/(2πRC).
Slope of the magnitude response beyond cut-off; about −20 dB/decade per pole, so second order gives −40 dB/decade.
Rejects frequencies in a band and passes frequencies below and above it; a narrow band-stop is a notch.
Maximally flat passband with monotonic fall; order N gives about −20N dB/decade roll-off.
Equiripple passband or stopband response; sharper transition than Butterworth for the same order.
One op-amp plus an RC network that realizes a second-order filter section; Q is set by resistor and capacitor ratios.
Two integrators and a summer in a loop give low-pass, band-pass and high-pass outputs at the same time.
MOS switches and a capacitor emulate a resistor R = 1/(fclk C), so cut-off scales with the clock frequency.
Comparator with positive feedback and two thresholds; it switches cleanly even with noise on the input.
Ramp wave with unequal charge and discharge times, giving a slow rise and fast reset or the reverse.
Circuit with no stable state; it oscillates continuously between two states without an external trigger.
Circuit with one stable state; one trigger produces one output pulse of a set width.
Circuit with two stable states; set and reset signals hold it in either state.
Timer IC containing two comparators, a latch, a discharge transistor and a 1/3 VCC, 2/3 VCC divider.
Feedback loop that compares input phase with VCO phase and drives the VCO until frequency and phase lock.
Oscillator whose output frequency is set by an external control voltage.
Binary-weighted input resistors create binary-weighted currents that are summed at an op-amp virtual ground.
DAC network using only R and 2R resistors to create binary-weighted currents; easy to match on an IC.
ADC that tests bits from MSB to LSB using a DAC and comparator; N cycles give an N-bit result.
ADC that oversamples and noise-shapes quantization error; high resolution at low signal bandwidth.

takeaways: An active filter uses an op-amp with resistors and capacitors to shape gain versus frequency without inductors.
A Bode plot reads a filter by its passband gain, cut-off frequency and roll-off slope.
Real filter specifications are met by choosing an approximation such as Butterworth or Chebyshev and then setting the required order.
A second-order section has a Q value, and a Sallen-Key circuit realizes that section with one op-amp.
A state-variable or universal filter gives low-pass, band-pass and high-pass outputs from the same circuit.
A switched-capacitor filter replaces resistors with clocked capacitors, so its cut-off is tuned by a clock ratio.
A comparator with hysteresis plus an integrator forms a square-triangle generator, and unequal charge paths make a sawtooth.
Astable, monostable and bistable multivibrators differ by the number of stable states and by how they leave a state.
The 555 timer uses a resistor divider, two comparators, a latch and a discharge transistor to set timing from two resistors and one capacitor.
A PLL locks a VCO to an input, and DAC and ADC architectures trade speed, resolution, accuracy and cost.
bank_note: Long answers usually expect the circuit, waveforms, design equations and a reasoned comparison of alternatives rather than only a block diagram.

bank.q: Draw an op-amp RC active low-pass filter and an active high-pass filter. Derive the transfer function, find the cut-off frequency, sketch the Bode magnitude plot and state the first-order roll-off.
outline: Bode plot showing passband and cut-off

bank.q: Compare Butterworth and Chebyshev filter responses. Explain how order, ripple and roll-off affect the choice for a given specification.
outline: Choice depends on ripple allowed and selectivity needed

bank.q: Explain the operation of astable, monostable and bistable multivibrators. Give the state conditions and output waveforms for each.
outline: Astable has no stable state and oscillates
Monostable has one stable state and one triggered pulse
Bistable has two stable states with set and reset
Waveforms and state table for each

bank.q: Explain the internal blocks of the 555 timer and the action of the comparators, latch and discharge transistor in astable and monostable modes.
outline: Three-resistor divider gives 1/3 VCC and 2/3 VCC
Two comparators set and reset the latch
Discharge transistor resets the timing capacitor
External R and C set timing

bank.q: Explain the blocks of a phase-locked loop. Define lock range and capture range, and describe how the VCO frequency follows the input.
outline: Phase detector, loop filter, VCO and feedback
Phase error drives VCO control voltage
Lock range and capture range definitions

bank.q: Design a second-order Sallen-Key low-pass filter for fc = 2 kHz and Q = 0.707 using equal capacitors. Show the design equations and select component values.
Using a state-variable filter, derive the low-pass, band-pass and high-pass outputs. Show how fc and Q are set, and choose R and C for fc = 1 kHz and Q = 5.
outline: Transfer functions for LP, BP and HP
fc set by integrator time constants
Q set by feedback resistor ratio

bank.q: Design a 555 astable multivibrator for 1 kHz and about 60% duty cycle. Derive R1, R2 and C, and explain why the basic circuit cannot give below 50% duty cycle.
outline: Basic duty cycle is always above 50%

bank.q: For an 8-bit R-2R ladder DAC with Vref = 5 V, calculate the output for input code 10110100 and find the LSB size. Discuss resistor matching errors.

Analyze a waveform generator made from a hysteresis comparator and an integrator. Derive the square and triangle waveforms, and find the frequency from the comparator thresholds and integrator time constant.
outline: Frequency depends on thresholds and RC

bank.q: Compare weighted-resistor and R-2R ladder DACs. Then explain how DAC settling time and ADC resolution affect a data-acquisition system.
outline: Weighted-resistor needs many accurate resistor values
R-2R uses only two values and suits ICs
ADC resolution and speed set measurement detail

bank.q: Analyze a switched-capacitor filter by showing that the switched capacitor behaves as R = 1/(fclk C). Explain clock tuning, aliasing and the comparison with active RC filters.
Evaluate Sallen-Key, state-variable and switched-capacitor filters for a narrow-band low-pass application. Discuss Q sensitivity, component tolerance, tuning and pick a suitable choice with reasons.
outline: Sallen-Key is simple but can have high Q sensitivity
State-variable gives several outputs and easier tuning
Switched-capacitor is clock-tunable but has aliasing and clock noise

bank.q: Analyze how a 555 monostable pulse width depends on R, C and comparator thresholds. Then explain how a PLL with a divider can multiply a 1 kHz reference to 10 kHz.
outline: PLL phase detector and VCO control
Divider in feedback sets frequency multiplication
Reasons for lock and stability limits

glossary.def: Filter built with an op-amp plus resistors and capacitors, so it can provide gain and avoid inductors.
Frequency at which the filter gain falls to 1/√2 of the passband gain, about −3 dB.
Rate at which gain falls beyond cut-off, usually stated in dB per decade or dB per octave.
Graph of magnitude or phase of a transfer function against frequency on a logarithmic frequency axis.
Filter approximation with a maximally flat passband and monotonic response.
Filter approximation with ripple in the passband or stopband and a sharper transition than Butterworth.
Number of poles in the filter transfer function; it sets the ultimate roll-off steepness.
Quality factor of a second-order section; it controls peaking near cut-off and damping.
Single-op-amp second-order active filter using an RC network and positive feedback.
Active filter using integrators and a summer to provide low-pass, band-pass and high-pass outputs together.
Active filter configuration that can produce several standard responses from the same circuit.
Active filter in which clocked capacitors replace resistors, making cut-off depend on the clock frequency.
Comparator with hysteresis, giving two switching thresholds and clean output transitions.
Oscillator circuit with no stable state that continuously switches between two states.
One-shot circuit with one stable state that produces a single pulse after a trigger.
Latch circuit with two stable states, set and reset by external signals.
Versatile timer IC used for astable and monostable timing, with comparators, latch and discharge transistor.
Control loop that locks a VCO to the phase and frequency of an input signal.
Oscillator whose frequency changes with an applied control voltage.
Digital-to-analog converter that turns a binary code into a proportional analog voltage or current.
DAC resistor network using only R and 2R values to create binary-weighted currents.
ADC that compares the input with many reference levels at once and encodes the result; very fast.
ADC that finds the output code bit by bit using a DAC, comparator and binary search.
ADC that integrates the input for a fixed time and then integrates a reference until zero; accurate but slower.
Oversampling ADC that uses noise shaping and digital filtering to obtain high resolution at low bandwidth.
